notes: Contour converts the frequency for a 48 kHz stream: the DAC designs every band for 24 kHz and plays it at the stream rate, so a band is written at half its frequency; a player that forces 44.1 kHz shifts every band about 8 % down (the editor offers 40-20000 Hz)

recognised by VID, PID and the literal USB product name: the unit reports "Kiwi Ears-Allegro Mini" (productName); devicePEQ also lists the spelling without the hyphen, kept as a name alias (nameAliases)

register layout: five bands, each a gain-and-frequency register and a Q-and-type register, consecutive from 0x26 (0x26-0x2F), read back on the unit (bench log allegro-mini-read-232520, run:2026-10-20-kiwi-ears-allegro-mini-05; scope-kt-walkplay.md:65; devicePEQ usbDeviceConfig.js, KT_0211L, baseRegisterOffset 0x26)
chip family KT_0211L (KTMicro); bcdDevice 0x0001; read on a PC without sending anything (run:2026-10-20-kiwi-ears-allegro-mini-05)
HID interface 3, report 0x4B with 10 data bytes (scope-kt-walkplay.md:52; run:2026-10-20-kiwi-ears-allegro-mini-05)

advBeta's KtMicro catalog has the Model PID 0x0111 while the kt0211 register map lists productIds {0x0113}; the unit seen here is 0x0111 (advbeta-reddit-astra@39c16e3:android/core/src/main/kotlin/io/github/chronosauros/contour/core/native/KtMicroCatalog.kt)

KTMicro register protocol: single 16-bit registers addressed by one byte, not the WalkPlay band frame; EQ enable register 0x24 (3 = on, 2 = off), SAVE 0x53, CLEAR 0x43, digital gain 0x66, Global Gain register 0x3B (scope-kt-walkplay.md)
gain +-12 dB and Q 0.1-10 are the vendor tool's values (another source lists +-10 dB and Q 0.1-5); the edges need a capture
Global Gain top is +3 dB (vendor step table 1..15 = -18..+3 dB, 13 = 0 dB); a 0 dB cap was an option; step 0 (possibly mute) needs a capture

driver.reconnectAfterSave stays "unknown" in the record (the code value true is held in PendingRecords) and the order of gain and frequency in a register write is not resolved from code reading: both need a capture of the vendor tool

reset.src: vendor web tool CLEAR (command 0x43); Contour ships no reset for any device (scope-kt-walkplay.md)

hwVolume.src: not examined for the Allegro Mini

rangesAccepted.note: Five PK bands were written in the acoustic runs (the register holds half the intended frequency for a 48 kHz stream); +-12 dB and Q 0.1-10 are the vendor web tool's values, read from its code, and the edges were not measured. LS and HS (codes 3 and 4) are held back.

acoustic.note: The DSP designs its RBJ biquads for 24 000 Hz and runs them at the stream rate (free fit 24 061 and 24 143 Hz, shift x1.84 at 44.1 kHz and x2.00 at 48 kHz). Below 8 kHz the model fits within 0.17 dB; a Q 5 band at register 6000 Hz plays wider than the model. At a 44.1 kHz stream every band plays 8.1 % lower than intended.

persistence.note: The EQ bands were not checked over a power cycle; the EQ switch and Global Gain kept their values after a replug.

settings.note: EQ switch OFF and ON and Global Gain 1, 15 and 13 each verified after the re-enumeration on a Pixel, and 13 to 12 to 13 written, saved and read back on the PC. A first phone run could not open the 10-byte HID report (fixed); on in every build since 2026-10-25.

tested.beyondVendor: The vendor web tool offers five PEQ bands, peak only. Contour adds the Global Gain output level (16 steps of 1.5 dB, -18..+3 dB), the EQ switch row and the frequency conversion for a 48 kHz stream; LS and HS stay held back until the vendor tool or a capture shows them.
